title: Steam methane reforming (SMR) reference family
objective: Optional literature-backed reference family for sanity-checking catalyst economics for steam reforming of natural gas, the dominant industrial hydrogen route. COMET itself remains reaction-agnostic and this family is a screening aid, not a process design.

balanced.label: Balanced
balanced.description: Balance economics, source confidence, route confidence, and performance.

cost-first.label: Cost-first
cost-first.description: Bias ranking toward selling cost while keeping route and evidence guardrails.

evidence-first.label: Evidence-first
evidence-first.description: Reward transparent, higher-confidence pricing and more reproducible routes.

route_templates.name: Ni impregnation on calcium aluminate with ring forming
preprocess: Calcium-aluminate or alpha-alumina carrier calcination and sizing
Nickel-nitrate solution make-up with Ca/K promoter dosing
synthesis: Impregnation of the carrier with the nickel solution
postprocess: In-situ reduction in the reformer (charged as NiO)
quality_gates: Crush strength for tall reformer tubes
route_templates.route_note: Century-scale industrial practice; commercial catalysts ship as shaped NiO and reduce in situ, so no reduction step is charged.

route_templates.name: Rh egg-shell impregnation for compact reformers
route_templates.manufacturing_mode: Egg-shell pellets or washcoated structured substrates
synthesis: Controlled egg-shell impregnation of Rh onto the outer shell
route_templates.route_note: Egg-shell control keeps costly Rh at the pellet exterior where the reaction runs; batch kiln matches the small compact-duty campaign scale.

route_templates.name: Sn/Ni surface-alloy impregnation
preprocess: Nickel and tin salt solution make-up
synthesis: Trace-tin co-impregnation targeting a surface alloy
postprocess: High-temperature reduction forming the Sn/Ni surface alloy
quality_gates: Carbon-limit spot test at low steam-to-carbon
route_templates.route_note: Same impregnation chain as the baseline plus a trace-metal step; the surface-alloy anneal is folded into the reduction.

candidates.title: Ni on calcium aluminate (industrial baseline)
candidates.summary: ~18-19 wt% NiO on a calcium-aluminate carrier with Ca/K additions - the tubular-reformer workhorse, run at 600-950 C and elevated pressure with steam-to-carbon control against coking.
decision_notes: The reference economics for hydrogen at scale: cheap metal, fully de-risked manufacture, lifetime governed by sintering/carbon/sulfur rather than catalyst price.
Composition basis: 18-19 wt% NiO rows documented in the cited characterization studies; K linkage to naphtha duty is industrial practice not re-verified from a primary abstract.

pricing.note: Contained-nickel basis of an ~18.5 wt% NiO loading with a mild precursor conversion markup.
2025e f.o.b. mine muriate-of-potash price, $600/t of K2O equivalent (USGS MCS Feb 2026).
Refractory calcium-aluminate carrier proxy, informed by the USGS alumina floor (~$0.27/lb) plus cement-chemistry processing; no public carrier-grade quote was verified.

candidates.title: Rh/Al2O3 compact-reformer route
candidates.summary: 0.5-2 wt% Rh on alumina for compact and membrane reformers: highest per-site activity in the Ru/Rh/Ni ranking, bought at rhodium prices and justified where reactor volume, not catalyst cost, dominates.
decision_notes: Pick when compactness or membrane integration outweighs metal cost; the small order size reflects the niche duty.
Loading screened at 1 wt% Rh, inside the 0.5-2 wt% band the compact-reformer literature documents.

pricing.note: Live Rh feed with a precursor conversion markup; loadings of 0.5-2 wt% are source-quoted for compact duty.
2025 USGS alumina import value used as a bulk oxide support proxy.

candidates.title: Sn/Ni surface alloy (coking-resistant)
candidates.summary: Trace tin alloyed into supported nickel suppresses carbon nucleation, extending stable operation at low steam-to-carbon ratios where the plain Ni baseline cokes.
decision_notes: The alloy-design answer to the baseline's carbon limit at nearly base-metal economics.
Sn and Ni loadings are screening assumptions (15 wt% Ni, 0.5 wt% Sn): the cited abstracts establish the trace-Sn surface-alloy strategy but do not state weight loadings.

pricing.note: Live Ni feed; loading is a screening assumption within normal reforming practice.
Live Sn feed (LME settlement via Westmetall, USGS MCS fallback) with a precursor / conversion markup; upgraded from the fixed USGS LME-average proxy.
2025 USGS alumina import value used as a bulk oxide support proxy.
